decisions.decision: The measured state, re-read by the coordinator at 76cfa91. The issuance table for all nine domain Requirement commands plus the release-bound completion: start-framing (from captured) ISSUED by Service.StartFraming, internal/application/framing.go:191; ready (from framing|waiting|needs-input) ISSUED by Service.AnswerHumanInput, human_input.go:648; needs-input (from framing|active|evaluating) ISSUED by Service.RequestHumanInput, human_input.go:519; start (from ready|recovering|waiting) NONE; wait (from ready|active|recovering) NONE; recover (from active|waiting) NONE; evaluate (from active) NONE; pause (from ready|active|waiting|recovering) NONE; cancel (from anything but completed|cancelled) NONE; domain.CompleteRequirementFromRelease (from evaluating) NONE. So six of the nine commands and the completion have no non-test issuer at all, and the set of Requirement statuses reachable through the application layer is exactly {captured, framing, needs-input, ready}. Separately, Service.Plan writes the parent Requirement WITHOUT any domain command: internal/application/service.go:936-941 appends an Increment id and increments Version directly, bypassing domain.DecideRequirement, and never touches Status.
decisions.rationale: Every figure is to be RE-MEASURED; the last eleven tasks each found a stale number. The premise handed to this task -- that internal/runner/orchestrator.go carries an Increment through Plan, Prepare, Claim and Start while the parent Requirement stays at captured -- is TRUE as written (orchestrator.go:41-116 does exactly that and never issues a Requirement command) but is incomplete in a way that changes the design: Orchestrator.RunFakeJourney has exactly ONE caller in the whole repository and it is internal/runner/orchestrator_test.go:56, and cmd/runner/main.go wires no control plane at all. So the only code that drives a whole journey is a test driver, and the defect is not that a production path leaves the parent behind but that no path advances it at all.

decisions.decision: The rule that decides whether an Increment's progress advances its parent EXISTS in the product documents, it is asymmetric, and it licenses exactly ONE parent transition. docs/architecture/domain-model.md:266 defines the Requirement status active as '1つ以上のIncrementが進行中' -- one or more Increments in progress. That is a definition, not a hint: the parent is active precisely because a subordinate Increment is in progress, so the start command (ready -> active) is licensed by Increment progress and by nothing else. In the opposite direction the documents refuse: domain-model.md:101 says '1 Requirementに複数Incrementを許す。Incrementが成功してもRequirementは自動完了しない。' -- an Increment succeeding does NOT auto-complete the Requirement; domain-model.md:272 defines completed as '対応Stable ReleaseとEvidenceで課題解決を確認'; docs/product/definition.md:104-105 makes completion 'Previewで実証され、Stableへ昇格した時点' and definition.md:130 forbids deciding completion by self-report. domain-model.md:292 adds that an abandoned Increment leaves the Requirement able to continue, and :382 that a handoff failure is an Execution failure and not a Requirement failure.
decisions.rationale: This is the measurement non_goals item 2 demands: 'do not advance a Requirement because a subordinate Increment moved, WITHOUT the rule that says it should'. The rule is quoted, so advancing to active is licensed; the counter-rules are quoted, so advancing to evaluating or completed is forbidden by the same documents. The remaining statuses are assigned by the same reading: domain-model.md:267 makes waiting '自動待機' on dependency, capacity and time -- the vocabulary internal/application/allocation.go:255-271 already exposes as scheduler.ReasonUnmetDependency and ReasonNoRunnerCapacity -- and :270 makes recovering 'lost ExecutionやPreview failureから再開中', which is internal/reconciler's subject. Both are automatic and neither has a caller, so neither belongs to a caller-initiated command. domain-model.md:269 makes paused '人間が処理を停止' and :273 makes cancelled '人間が以後の解決を不要と判断', and definition.md:147 lists 'cancel requirement' as a required human control. So the seven unissued transitions have four different issuer classes, which is the basis of d3.

decisions.decision: SPLIT. All seven transitions in ONE task is refused, and V2-084 keeps exactly the two edges that make the Increment-driven rule real: a new caller command issuing ready from framing, and the start transition issued inside the transaction that puts an Increment into progress. The other five, and the completion, become follow-ons whose outcomes are written in d10; the coordinator issues their ids.
decisions.rationale: The split is forced by measurement, not by size. (i) pause is a TRAP today: internal/domain/model.go:434-445 declares no resume command, and RequirementReadyCommand is admitted from framing, waiting and needs-input but NOT from paused (model.go:481), so the only exit from paused is cancel. domain-model.md:269 says the exit should be '直前の安全な非終端状態', which needs a stored previous status that domain.Requirement does not have. Issuing pause without an exit would create a one-way door, and adding the exit requires editing internal/domain, which non_goals item 1 forbids. STOP and record. (ii) completion is UNREACHABLE by construction, not merely unissued: domain.CompleteRequirementFromRelease requires a domain.StableReleaseProof whose only constructor is domain.CompletePromotionWithProof (internal/domain/release.go:150), reached only through release.PromotionGate, which is reached only through release.Pipeline.Promote -- and Pipeline.Promote has ZERO non-test callers anywhere in internal/application, internal/api or cmd. So no running process can obtain the input, and evaluate would move a Requirement into a status nothing can leave. STOP and record. (iii) wait and recover have no caller at all: their issuer is the bounded reconcile tick (docs/architecture/technology.md:162-170), which lives in internal/reconciler and today takes no application.Caller -- and whether it can even hold a scheduler identity is V2-086's question, not this one's. (iv) cancel is deliverable and clean but it is an owner control verb whose design must also decide what a Control Intent with mode cancel scoped to a Requirement does, which is a control-plane design of its own. Four issuer classes, four evidence sets, and two of them blocked on measurements this task can only record: one task would have to lie about at least two of them.

decisions.decision: Edge one: Service.CompleteFraming, a new caller command in the EXISTING file internal/application/framing.go, issuing domain.RequirementReadyCommand from RequirementFraming. It follows Service.StartFraming's discipline exactly: callerActor(ctx, RoleOwner, RoleScheduler); requireRequest; requestFingerprint("complete-framing", req); s.mutate(ctx, "complete-framing:"+req.RequestID, ...) with u.Idempotency(ctx, req.RequestID, "complete-framing"), the fingerprint-conflict refusal and restoreResponse replay; the ControlTarget and revision resolved inside the transaction from u.RequirementRepositoryLink and domain.EffectiveControl; domain.Permit with Kind domain.PermitClaim and NOTHING passed to domain.EffectFromPermit; domain.DecideRequirement with ExpectedVersion from the request; u.SaveRequirement; s.record with event type requirement.ready; and NO outbox item. One route, POST /v1/requirements/{requirement_id}:complete-framing, added by the same prefix-plus-suffix idiom as :start-framing (internal/api/api.go:454-472, suffix constant beside startFramingSuffix at api.go:609), gated to RoleOwner or RoleScheduler, declared in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml.
decisions.rationale: Measured reason this edge is needed at all: domain.RequirementReadyCommand's only issuer is AnswerHumanInput (human_input.go:648), so the ONLY way a Requirement can reach ready today is for someone to ask it a question and for the owner to answer -- ready, the status internal/application/allocation.go:373 calls 'the only schedulable status', is otherwise unreachable from framing. domain-model.md:265 defines ready as '優先順位評価済みで実行可能', which is the completion of framing, so the edge the domain already admits from framing is exactly the right one and no domain change is needed. The kind is PermitClaim for the same reason V2-082 d5 chose it for start-framing and the same reason dp-v2-085 d2 chose it for Plan and Prepare: docs/product/definition.md:142-143 makes pause-intake 'take no new work in, finish what you already have' and pause-claim 'stop claiming new work', and declaring an already-framed Requirement executable is the moment it becomes claimable. The resulting seven-mode table is therefore identical to start-framing's: allow and pause-intake ALLOW, the other five DENY.

decisions.decision: Edge two: the start transition is issued INSIDE Service.Claim's existing transaction, derived from the claimed Increment's own parent, and is NOT a separate caller command. After domain.DecideIncrement succeeds, Claim reads the parent Requirement by inc.RequirementID, and: if its status is RequirementReady it issues domain.DecideRequirement with Kind domain.RequirementStart and ExpectedVersion taken from the value read in the SAME transaction (never from the request) and saves it; if the status is already RequirementActive it does nothing, because 'one or more Increments in progress' is already true and a second claim must be idempotent with respect to the parent; if the status is anything else it does nothing and the claim proceeds exactly as today.
decisions.rationale: The rule quoted in d2 makes active a DERIVED property of Increment progress, so its issuer must be the transaction that creates the progress, not a second command a caller could forget. Service.Claim is the right transaction on three measurements: it is the point where an Increment leaves ready and an Execution and Lease are created; it is already permit-gated with domain.PermitClaim AND routed through domain.EffectFromPermit (service.go:1228 and the effectOutbox at :1669-1673), so the parent transition inherits the strictest gate in the system -- denied under every non-allow mode -- with no new permit; and it is reached by a caller a real transport produces, the Runner from internal/api/auth.go:50. Deriving the parent's expected version from the in-transaction read rather than from ClaimRequest is the same rule V2-082 d6 applied to the control revision: a caller must not be able to make a derived transition fail for a reason unrelated to its intent, and ClaimRequest gains no field. The third branch -- do nothing when the parent is neither ready nor active -- is what keeps the change ADDITIVE, and it is the subject of d6.

decisions.decision: Claim does NOT refuse an Increment whose parent is not ready or active. The refusal is the right end state and it is NOT taken here: it is recorded as a measured, LOGGED residual and assigned to the follow-on in d10. What this task asserts instead is the positive half -- that a Requirement driven captured -> framing -> ready and then claimed becomes active, and that a second claim leaves it active -- plus a logged measurement that a claim against a captured parent still succeeds.
decisions.rationale: Measured blast radius of the refusal: 18 test files across five packages call Claim (15 hits in internal/application/service_test.go, 8 in internal/runner/provider_live_test.go, and hits in internal/reconciler, internal/store/firestore and internal/runner), and essentially all of them capture, plan, prepare and claim without ever framing, so their parents are captured. Refusing would break every one of them and would require editing three files that queued tasks hold (internal/api/api_test.go is V2-087's, internal/application/repository_test.go is V2-087's, internal/application/service.go is V2-083's). A change that rewrites 18 fixtures in five packages is not additive and cannot be verified as leaving existing behaviour intact in the same task that introduces the two new edges. The residual is LOGGED rather than asserted for exactly the reason V2-082 gave when it left Plan and Prepare logged (internal/application/framing_test.go:562-564): asserting a defect pins it in place and turns its repair into a failure in a file the repairing task may not own.

decisions.decision: internal/domain is not edited. No RequirementCommandKind, no RequirementStatus, no PermitKind, no allowed() list change. The reachable Requirement status set goes from {captured, framing, needs-input, ready} to exactly {captured, framing, needs-input, ready, active}, and the five still-unissued transitions plus the completion stay unissued.
decisions.rationale: Measured: internal/domain/model.go:480-484 already admits RequirementReadyCommand from RequirementFraming and sets RequirementReady, and model.go:485-489 already admits RequirementStart from RequirementReady and sets RequirementActive. So both edges are calls, not model changes. M1's closure proof over domain.DecideRequirement is unaffected because no reachable status set inside the domain changes, whereas any domain edit would have to re-establish it. This is also the honesty check on the size of the repair: a lifecycle step that needs no domain change cannot have widened the state machine.

decisions.decision: No read model change. internal/application/readmodels.go is prohibited BY DESIGN. nextAction (readmodels.go:306-329) branches on completed and cancelled, then on Execution status, then on Increment status, then on whether the Increment list is empty; ready and active enter none of those branches, so a Requirement in either continues to report exactly what it reports today. RequirementDetailView.Status already carries any valid status.
decisions.rationale: Measured at readmodels.go:306-329. The consequence is that the repair is observable through the field the existing dogfood and owner console already read, with no new field and no new key in any response -- which is what makes the openapi change a pure path addition rather than a schema change, and what keeps internal/web out of this task entirely.

decisions.decision: The proof is split by what this task's authorisations can execute, and each part says what it does and does not establish. (1) Over the composed api.Handler with the in-memory store, the full chain is asserted in one run: capture -> :start-framing -> :complete-framing -> detail reports ready -> Plan -> Prepare -> Claim as a runner -> detail reports the parent ACTIVE with its version incremented by exactly one -> a second Claim on a second Increment leaves the parent active. (2) Against the REAL cmd/control-plane binary and the REAL Firestore emulator over real HTTP, TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive is extended to capture, :start-framing, :complete-framing and read the detail back reporting ready -- the segment that needs no runner enrolment. (3) The claim-to-active segment against real persistence is NOT executed, because internal/api/live_local_test.go has no runner enrolment, and that boundary is stated rather than blurred. No Provider CLI is started and TestFoundationPreviewLocalDogfood is not run.
decisions.rationale: Measured constraint that forces the split: internal/api/live_local_test.go composes LocalOwnerBearerAuthenticator from AGENTIC_LOOP_LOCAL_OWNER_TOKENS and drives owner-authenticated routes only, exactly as dp-v2-082 d10 recorded; Claim requires a verified runner session. So the segment real persistence can prove is the owner-driven half, and that is the honest boundary. Part (1) is a real HTTP surface with real role gates and is the only place the whole chain is asserted in one run.

decisions.decision: The follow-on outcomes, for the coordinator to issue ids for. (F1) 'Stop an Increment from being claimed while its Requirement is not recorded as executable, and bring every fixture that claims one onto the lifecycle the domain models instead of exempting it.' (F2) 'Give the owner the two verbs the product promises for a Requirement -- pause it and cancel it -- including the exit from paused that the domain does not yet model, so pausing is not a one-way door, and decide what a Control Intent scoped to a Requirement with mode cancel does to that Requirement.' (F3) 'Let the bounded reconcile tick say why a Requirement is not moving: give waiting and recovering the automatic issuer the architecture names for them, so a Requirement blocked on a dependency or holding a lost Execution stops being reported as active.' (F4) 'Make a Requirement completable by wiring the promotion its proof comes from, so evaluating and completed stop being statuses no running process can produce.' Dependency order: F1 after V2-084; F2 needs a domain edit and must be its own task; F3 after V2-086, which decides whether the tick can hold an identity; F4 after F3 and after the release pipeline is wired, and it is an M8-adjacent task, not an M5 one.
decisions.rationale: Each outcome names the measurement that blocks it so the next tech lead does not have to re-derive it: F1 the 18 claiming test files, F2 the absent resume command and the absent previous-status field, F3 the reconciler's lack of a Caller, F4 that release.Pipeline.Promote has no non-test caller so domain.StableReleaseProof cannot be obtained in a running process. Writing them here is what stops V2-084's evidence from having to claim more than it did.

decisions.decision: Quota and determinism are constraints on the proof, not afterthoughts. Both new writes fit inside quota.MutationUsage (Reads 32 / Writes 16, internal/quota/quota.go:62): CompleteFraming writes the Requirement, the event and the idempotency record, and Claim's added parent transition is one more read and one more write inside a reservation Capture already proves fits the same pair of reads. The in-memory adapter never calls quota.Counter.TrueUp, so quota.ReadTransactionUsage (Reads 6001 / Writes 1, quota.go:56) admits only FOUR read transactions per budget day against quota.DefaultBudget's 25000 reads -- and d9's chain reads the detail route at least four times. The injected clock is advanced between reads; no assertion is weakened, no read is dropped and no budget is raised.
decisions.rationale: Measured: s.transact reserves ReadTransactionUsage once per read transaction (service.go:122-133) and internal/store/memory/store.go:167-169 forwards Reserve without a true-up, so the fifth read of a fixed clock day fails with ErrOverBudget. A test author who does not know this will either drop a read or weaken an assertion, both of which destroy the proof. That adapter defect is V2-087's and is not fixed here.

verification: devbox run --pure -e AGENTIC_LOOP_LIVE_LOCAL=1 -- scripts/firestore-emulator.sh go test -count=1 -v -run TestControlPlanePreviewLocalLive ./internal/api
risks: d2 is the load-bearing decision and it rests on reading a definition table as normative. If the implementer reads docs/architecture/domain-model.md:266 differently -- for instance concluding that 'one or more Increments in progress' describes a state rather than licensing a transition -- that is a design disagreement, not an implementation detail: stop and escalate. Do NOT resolve it by advancing the parent on some other Increment event, and do NOT resolve it by adding a caller command for start, which would let a caller assert that work is in progress when none is.

The temptation d6 creates is to add the refusal because it is obviously right. It would break 18 test files across five packages and three of those files are held by queued tasks. The residual is logged, not asserted, and it is F1's to repair.

Editing Service.Claim is editing the most heavily asserted command in the system: 18 test files drive it and its permit and fencing behaviour is pinned by internal/application/stop_matrix_test.go and internal/reconciler's journeys. The added parent transition must be the last thing in the callback before the existing record call, must not change any existing return value, and must not alter the outbox item. If any existing assertion moves, the change was not additive.

internal/application/service.go is held by V2-083 and by V2-085; internal/api/api.go by V2-083; internal/api/api_test.go by V2-087; internal/application/framing_test.go by V2-085. This task must be serialized after all of them, and it is the last of the four.

contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml is a bundle api-contract role member and the contracts component root, so editing it moves both the contracts component key and the release BundleDigest. That is expected. What must not happen is writing any digest value into a document.

Two of the seven transitions this task's outcome names are blocked by measurements rather than by scope -- pause has no exit the domain models, and completion's proof object has no producer in any running process. An implementer under pressure to deliver 'the rest of a Requirement's life' may be tempted to add a domain edge or to fabricate a proof. Both are stop-and-escalate conditions, and the evidence must record them as blocked with the measurement that blocks them.
